title: SAT Solver Selection: Move Beyond Handcrafted Features

problem.claim: SAT solver selection is needed because no single SAT solver dominates across all problem instances.

gap.claim: Traditional SAT solver selection methods rely on computationally expensive handcrafted features that require extensive domain expertise.

contributions.claim: F2S3 provides an end-to-end feature-free approach for SAT solver selection.

The approach transforms problem instances into graph data, refines higher-order structural properties and node relationships, enhances graph features with a dual-proximity representation, and projects them into low-dimensional vectors.
A Sensitive-Associative Cascade Forest performs solver selection through classification.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method is reported to capture the structural complexity of graph data, eliminate handcrafted features, and improve feature representation in low-dimensional space.
Experiments on the ASlib database dataset are reported to show consistent outperformance over state-of-the-art SAT solver selection approaches.
The method is reported to achieve higher gap values while requiring less computation time than approaches using manually computed features.

narrative_sequence.summary: SAT is presented as a foundational problem supporting many applications.
Because solver performance varies by instance, machine learning is used to select solvers dynamically.
Existing selection methods depend on expensive handcrafted features and domain expertise.
F2S3 uses graph representations, structural refinement, dual-proximity features, low-dimensional projection, and cascade-forest classification.
The authors report improved representation and stronger dataset performance with lower computation time than manually featured approaches.

source_observation.claim: The proposed pipeline replaces handcrafted features with graph-based representations and learned low-dimensional features.

interpretation.claim: End-to-end representation learning may reduce dependence on domain-specific feature engineering when instance structure can be encoded as a graph.

application.claim: For algorithm-selection tasks with expensive handcrafted descriptors, evaluate graph-based end-to-end representations as an alternative.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported SAT solver selection setting or ASlib dataset.

source_observation.claim: The method combines structural graph processing with a cascade-forest classifier for solver selection.

interpretation.claim: Combining structure-preserving representation learning with a downstream selector may improve algorithm-selection performance while controlling feature computation cost.

application.claim: Consider preserving higher-order relationships before classification in structured algorithm-selection problems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide ablations showing which pipeline component is responsible for the reported improvements.

unknowns: No dataset size, solver set, baselines, or experimental protocol is specified.
No numerical performance results or definition of the reported gap values is provided.
No details are given about training cost, model architecture, or reproducibility.
